question.text: One of the stated purposes of NPO registration on SSE is to bring interested NPOs onto a 'common platform of legal requirements'. As SIA, Mr. Arjun Desai is explaining this to Nari Shakti Trust. Which of the following BEST captures the rationale?

answer.text: To force all NPOs to re-register under the Companies Act 2013 as Section 8 Companies
To bring NPOs of varied legal structures onto a common platform of legal requirements for SSE access, without disturbing their underlying registration as trusts, societies or Section 8 companies
To replace state-level charity commissioners with a central SEBI office
To mandate that all NPOs obtain ISO 9001 certification

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 76 explains that NPOs have varied legal structures and that registration brings them onto a common platform of legal requirements for the purposes of accessing the SSE. Pages 77-78 list the qualifying legal forms — trusts, state-law trusts, societies and Section 8 companies — that NPOs may already hold. The harmonisation works at the SSE-access layer; NPOs keep their existing legal form. The Trap: Option A wrongly forces re-registration as Section 8 companies, option C wrongly replaces state-level charity bodies with a central SEBI office, and option D introduces an ISO 9001 mandate that is not part of the SSE framework. Each contradicts the harmonisation-without-re-registration design. Note: The keyed answer is grounded in pages 76-78; no anecdote about SSE officials misinterpreting state-law trusts is needed to settle it.
